title: The Last Person Still Looking
thesis: When information defeats the expected substitute for an independently required inquiry without affecting current evidential support for its answer, an agent can be required to restore investigation while retaining the same rational confidence.
contribution: A focused synthesis linking a policy-indexed forecast condition on withdrawal to a precise diagnosis of inquiry repair without belief revision; distinguishes support for a forecast, sufficiency of forecasted performance, and realized success, and tests departure-triggered replacements and conditional permission policies.
strongest_objection: A sophisticated combination of instrumental inquiry norms and existing coverage conditions can derive the argument, so its explanatory and competitive significance may be modest even if the distinctions are correct.
originality_limitations: The search was bounded and excerpt-based. Full Dunn and Arielli works were unavailable. An equivalent transition-and-repair constraint may already appear in wider literature. The manuscript does not claim historical priority or a new foundation for normativity.
open_questions: Does the broader literature on epistemic free riding already state an equivalent argument?
Which independently justified requirements of inquiry provide the most substantial applications of the conditional resumption result?
How should responsibilities for restoring an inquiry be fairly allocated after a permissibly risky policy fails?
How much information about a changing organization is needed for an adequate prospective forecast?
